label: late copy phase (step >= 10) of long sequences, favoring inputs m/t/x/k/d/r/1/e
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (after the step right after <DEL>, so recall_idx >= 1), and almost only at absolute step t >= 10. That means it is effectively limited to long sequences: L=9 holds 76% of activation mass and L=8 holds 20%, with nothing for L <= 5. Silent during the original phase and at the delimiter step. Within that window the firing rate rises over time: about 15-21% at t=10-12 and 35-43% at t=16-17, and the largest activations sit at the last copy steps of L=9 sequences. Which token is being fed back in also matters: m (the strongest), t, x, k, d, r, 1 and e have well above average rates, while o, z, j and y are low. The window (copy phase, t>=10) alone has recall 0.99 but precision 0.19. Adding the token set gives dev F1 0.52, and widening the token set or adding a late-step clause did not raise F1 above 0.52. This looks like a graded code for time step and copied token, not a crisp detector.
